My pc runs great but makes a lot of heat in my small room (makes my room hot, not a big deal this time year but sucks in the summer). Might be fun to do diy liquid cooling and maybe I could push the heat out the window. Tips?

-AMD 7950 GPU

-AMD FX-6300 CPU

Have you done liquid cooling before? If not I'd recommend getting your feet wet (heh) with a closed loop system. Corsair makes some serviceable easy to use ones like the H100i that are a good place to start. That would let you play with how to setup fans for a radiator and so on. I've got a couple of friends started this way before moving on to DIY and dealing with reservoirs, fittings and so on.

As far as dumping the heat outside, the main issue is likely to be the length of tubing required. Assuming you want the radiator fans venting directly outdoors (and given that this makes sense with indoor/outdoor temps), unless the PC is right by a window you'll need some long tubes. You add liquid the more tubing you need which means more work for the pump, larger reservoir, and more potential for leaks. It can definitely be done, but it wouldn't be a first timer project I think.

Have you considered maybe "cooling" the air that is released into the room instead? For example you might have fresh air intake in your wind tunnel so that it isn't like a space heater at your feet or whatever. You could also look at doing a refrigerated system with compressor, etc. I did a hack with a little dorm fridge that worked great in a small room with poor airflow. Just tossing out some general ideas here. I'm no expert but I have been doing custom air and liquid cooling CPU and GPU for a couple decades now so I'm glad to help if I can.
The pc is 5 feet (2.5 meters) away from the window but maybe I could move it closer

That's not a super long way, so it might not be too bad - however I've only ever done anything that length and over on aquarium setups, not PC cooling. I can tell you that you would need to consider 2 things up front: 1) head pressure of the pump to the lift required and 2) speed of coolant movement. For 1, a pump pushes the coolant and it will have a rating as to how much it can lift the fluid over its own height - distance isn't that important here it is more about if you are having to go from the floor up to a window for example. Keep in mind you have to get it back as well. Also, you want as straight a shot as possible - any turns and bends will reduce your flow - significantly. 2 is a bit more complicated but basically the longer the distance the more the fluid slows down. To get around this you probably would want to use 2 pumps. One pushing the coolant away from the heat source as you expect, and a second pushing the cooled fluid back. So you might need 2 reservoirs, one inside one outside. There are push/pull pump setups as well but I'm not sure how they work exactly - I just know if you make a long run (I setup one that was about 25 feet for several aquariums) you can end up starving the pump at the far end making it 'pull' which it isn't designed to do and you can burn it out, get cavitation, etc.

Anyway this is getting too wordy so I'll just say if you could put it right by the window, mount the radiator just outside with fans in push/pull on either side and proper spacing you'd likely be okay. Now this would probably not work once it warmed up again as your radiator would be getting heated at that point. You could put the reservoir in a little fridge to help cool it perhaps? In any case depending on humidity in your area you might get condensation on your tubes so consider that as well. Sorry if I confused you any - I'm rambling a bit...side effect of keeping a limber mind...
